items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: And from then on Art and I became very, very close

ctx.x: When you first heard Art was he playing already in that same...
When I first heard Art I didn't think he could play as well as Lannie Scott. I first met Lannie in Shreveport. But I learned my lesson. Art Tatum is...well,

when I first heard him in Chicago, Earl Hines...well, I went to this after-hours spot and Lovey Taylor said to me, said to Earl Hines, "Earl, there's a kid in town playing the piano. Like to hear him?" Earl said, "No, I don't want to hear nobody." So Art Tatum started playing "Tiger Rag," you know...it was just amazing. You just couldn't believe that one man could play that fast, or do as much, or had as much...was ambidextrous or musically developed beyond, you know, the descriptions, he was just so amazing. And…
